biography: Alan Bonner, a name synonymous with grit and calculation in the Ultima GTR racing circuit, hails from the unassuming town of Brackley, England. His journey began not on the track, but in his father's small garage, elbows deep in engine grease. He spent his teenage years rebuilding a derelict Mini Cooper, a project that ignited his passion for speed and engineering. A pivotal moment came during a local hill climb event when, against all odds, Bonner, in his cobbled-together Mini, outpaced seasoned racers in far superior machinery. This victory was the validation he needed, and he invested every penny into securing a seat in a Ginetta Junior championship. While he never reached the heights of Formula 1, Bonner carved a niche for himself in the world of GT racing, becoming a fixture in the Ultima GTR series. Now, nearing the twilight of his career, he is respected as a veteran, known for his tactical prowess and unwavering determination, even if raw pace isn't always on his side.
drivingStyle: Bonner is not a driver known for flamboyant overtakes or daring maneuvers. His style is one of meticulous planning and relentless consistency. He is a master of tire management, often nursing his rubber through long stints while others fade. His cornering technique is precise, favoring smooth lines and minimal wheel spin. He thrives under pressure, rarely cracking, and is adept at exploiting the smallest weaknesses in his opponents. Bonner is a tactical driver, a chess player on wheels, always thinking several moves ahead.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about making the right choices at the right time. It's a game of probabilities, and I intend to play it better than anyone else."
careerHighlight: Winning the Spa 24 Hours in 2016 with the Ultima GTR team, securing a hard-fought victory after a grueling race plagued by mechanical issues and inclement weather. Bonner's strategic tire management in the final stint proved decisive.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2019 Nürburgring 24 Hours, a mistake that cost his team a likely victory and left Bonner deeply disappointed.
